headline: DevOps Engineer | Cloud Engineer | Linux System Administrator
summary: Cloud and DevOps Engineer trained through the NTI Cloud DevOps Accelerator, with hands-on experience in AWS (EC2, VPC, IAM), Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD with Jenkins and GitHub Actions, and Linux administration. Built end-to-end cloud-native projects, from infrastructure provisioning and GitOps delivery to security and monitoring, with a focus on automation, security, and scalable system design.

bullets.text: Built the final project, an end-to-end pipeline on AWS that provisions infrastructure with Terraform and Ansible, builds and scans images with Jenkins, SonarQube and Trivy, and deploys to EKS with Helm, monitored with Prometheus, Grafana and Loki.
Delivered two end-to-end CI/CD pipelines for a 3-service application on EKS, one with Jenkins and Ansible and one with GitHub Actions (OIDC) and ArgoCD GitOps.

bullets.label: Platform & Security
bullets.text: Five Python/FastAPI banking microservices and an NGINX frontend on EKS, built for financial correctness (fencing tokens, row-lock ordering). Versioned Terraform modules deploy through GitHub Actions (OIDC) and ArgoCD App-of-Apps, secured with default-deny NetworkPolicies, Istio mTLS, Gateway API and External Secrets Operator (IRSA).

bullets.label: Delivery, Streaming & Reliability
bullets.text: Trivy-scanned, Cosign-signed images are promoted by GitOps PRs and released as Argo Rollouts canaries gated on Prometheus metrics. Strimzi Kafka (KRaft, TLS/SCRAM, ACLs, dead-letter queue) carries events; Pytest concurrency tests, Prometheus/Grafana/Loki observability, and a disaster recovery drill rebuilt the cluster in 23 min 50 s with Multi-AZ RDS.

bullets.label: Infrastructure & Access
bullets.text: Enterprise-style RHEL environment on EC2 (VPN gateway, control, identity, utility and per-team workstations) in private subnets behind a NAT gateway, built with modular Terraform; reachable only through a WireGuard VPN with per-team ranges, firewalld and default-deny security groups.

bullets.label: Automation & Operations
bullets.text: Idempotent Ansible roles (EC2 dynamic inventory) handle SSH hardening, SELinux, firewalld, chrony and fleet patching; Bash scripts rebuild and test the lab, with tickets, runbooks and incident reports documenting changes.

Jenkins multi-branch pipelines for containerized apps on EKS with SonarQube and Trivy quality gates, on Terraform-provisioned infrastructure configured by Ansible; Prometheus, Grafana, and Loki cover metrics and logs.

Modular Terraform for a 3-tier AWS app (VPC, ALBs, Auto Scaling groups, RDS) with tier-isolated security groups, deployed through a Jenkins pipeline with a manual approval gate and monitored by CloudWatch alarms.

Serverless CI/CD for a 3-service app on EKS: GitHub Actions authenticates through OIDC with no stored AWS keys, secrets sync from AWS Secrets Manager, and ArgoCD keeps the cluster in sync with Git; monitored with Prometheus and Grafana.

paragraphs: I am applying for the DevOps Engineer role at Nilecode Systems in Cairo. I build cloud platforms as code and prove they recover, from Terraform and EKS to GitOps delivery, and I hold the AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate certification.

Your posting asks for AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes and CI/CD. In my Nexora core banking project I provisioned the VPC, EKS and RDS MySQL from versioned Terraform modules, and delivered through GitHub Actions, which assumes AWS IAM roles through OIDC, and ArgoCD GitOps. A disaster recovery drill deleted the EKS cluster and rebuilt it to a healthy application in 23 minutes 50 seconds, against a 30-minute RTO target. For Linux administration, my RHEL 10 lab on AWS uses modular Terraform and idempotent Ansible roles, with every host hardened to OpenSCAP CIS Level 1 at 100%.

I like owning the path from a commit to a running, observable service, and making that path safe enough that a release can be rolled back by a metric instead of a person. In Nexora, an Argo Rollouts canary aborts if the Prometheus 5xx error rate exceeds 5%. I would bring that approach to Nilecode Systems, and I would welcome a conversation about your platform.

email_body:
Hello,

I am applying for the DevOps Engineer role at Nilecode Systems in Cairo.
My CV and cover letter are attached. They cover my work with AWS, Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD and Linux administration.
I would be glad to discuss the role.
why_this_role: This role matches the work I did in Nexora, where I provisioned AWS infrastructure with Terraform, delivered to EKS through GitHub Actions and ArgoCD, and proved recovery with a 23 minute 50 second rebuild drill.
